chapter_title: The Chapter of the Commandments of Righteousness
chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by institutional/disciplinary instruction (elect vs. catechumens, fasting/alms, giving persons to the church, building projects), introduced with a formulaic dialogue frame. The strong editorial fatigue signal matches the heavy pastoral drift in the second half. Even where Manichaean technical terms occur (e.g., Cross of Light; sun and moon as light-givers), they function inside prescriptive community rules rather than impersonal cosmological mechanism. ¶7 is an editorial seam-like extension focused on catechumenal contributions to the holy church; it is entirely late pastoral material.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Begins with explicit hagiographic dialogue attribution (“[Once more] the enlightener speaks to his disciples”), and the content is a prescriptive summary of ‘righteousness’ (continence, ‘rest of the hands,’ dietary rules) rather than impersonal cosmological exposition. Cross of Light appears as a rule-context term (avoid harming vegetation/light-soul), not a systematic cosmological mapping.

Continues as ethical/institutional exhortation about dispensing wisdom/faith/grace to others; no cosmological mechanics, no structured degree-map. The voice is paraenetic (“he should do… he can give…”), fitting later community instruction.

Programmatic institutional distinction (elect vs. catechumen) and ‘two stages’ perfection language; functions as a rubric/transition into catechumen rules. High Christian/pastoral register; no core cosmological structure.

Explicit catechumenate obligations (fasting/prayer/almsgiving) and ‘lord’s day’ phrasing mark church discipline. Prayer to sun and moon is framed as a rule of practice, not as an old explanatory cosmology.
Institutional economy of merit: giving a child/relative/slave ‘to the church’ and sharing in good works—clear community administrative/pastoral material.
Building dwellings/places ‘in the holy church’ as alms is straightforward institutional instruction; no detachable older teaching content.

Seam-flagged editorial extension: reiterates ‘three works/alms’ and amplifies benefits ‘in the holy church’ with heavy catechumenal/institutional vocabulary. Entire paragraph reads as an editor’s expansion of catechumen policy and reward language, not inherited cosmological teaching.
